open_obligations: Identify exactly which of these restrictions Proposition 7 relaxes (e.g. deterministic prover strategies or verifiers built from convex combinations of deterministic functions).
Check that the adp protocol matches Anil et al.'s formulation.
Do not read this as refuting Anil et al.'s theorem within its stated assumptions.
out.other_title: PVG: verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium iff complete and sound protocol
out.rationale: Anil et al. prove verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria are necessary and sufficient for complete and sound protocols under their assumptions (realizable complete and sound verifier, instance revealed after the verifier commits). Hammond and Adam-Day say Anil et al.'s adp correspondence holds when prover strategies are deterministic functions from inputs to messages and verifier strategies are convex combinations of deterministic decision functions, and that relaxing these restrictions means the correspondence no longer holds. Their Proposition 7 gives a probabilistic decision problem and adp game where, although a valid proof with completeness error 0 exists, being a verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium is neither necessary nor sufficient for validity.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibria of prover-verifier games correspond to valid proofs once Anil et al.'s restrictions are relaxed

text: The authors argue that the restrictions under which Anil et al.'s Abstract Decision Problem (adp) protocol has an equilibrium-validity correspondence limit its power, and that relaxing them breaks the correspondence. Proposition 7 states that there is a probabilistic decision problem and an adp game where, although a valid interactive proof with completeness error 0 exists, being a verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium is neither necessary nor sufficient for validity.
title: Proposition 7: equilibria of the adp prover-verifier game need not be valid proofs
